name: Higgsfield
h1: Higgsfield ARR: $100M in Six Months, a $5.4B Valuation by Year Two.
intro: Higgsfield put cinematic camera motion — crash zooms, bullet time, crane shots — into consumer AI video generation, and monetized it with plain subscriptions. Two months after launch it was already at $11M ARR; six months in it crossed $100M; by 2026 a $400M Series B valued it at $5.4B. Every publicly reported number, with sources, is below.

modelTitle: Camera Moves Nobody Else Had, Sold as Subscriptions.
modelParagraphs: Higgsfield's wedge was motion control: presets like bullet time, crash zoom and crane shots that made AI video look like it was shot with real camera rigs, at a moment when most generators returned static, drone-like clips. That specificity — a film-school feature list rather than a generic text-to-video box — is what turned social creators into paying subscribers within weeks of launch.

Revenue comes from consumer subscription tiers plus credit packs for renders, the standard consumer-AI stack. The paid funnel is powered by the product's own output: every cinematic clip posted to TikTok or Instagram is an ad, which is how the company reached millions of monthly actives on unusually short timelines. The Soul image model and sketch-to-image tools widened the subscription beyond video.
revenueMix: Monthly and annual tiers for video and image generation.
Pay-as-you-go renders on top of subscription allowances.
Output posted to social doubles as acquisition, keeping paid-UA share efficient.

faqs.a: Higgsfield crossed $100M annualized run rate roughly six months after launching, in late 2025. Exact current revenue has not been disclosed since; treat anything above $100M as an estimate pending the next company milestone.

faqs.q: How Did Higgsfield Grow So Fast?
faqs.a: A specific product wedge (cinematic camera-motion presets), a consumer subscription with a free tier, and organic distribution through the clips its own users post to social media. Two months post-launch it reported $11M ARR and more than 2M monthly active users.
A $400M Series B in 2026 valued the company at $5.4B, up from the $50M round announced in September 2025 alongside its $50M ARR milestone.
Alex Mashrabov, former Head of Generative AI at Snap, founded the company in 2023. The founding thesis was controllable motion for AI video rather than generic text-to-video generation.
Consumer subscriptions for video and image generation, supplemented by credit packs for additional renders. Free-tier output circulates on social platforms and doubles as the acquisition channel.
